commentary.heading: Wall Street slides despite Anthropic's record debut
commentary.body: US shares fell sharply on Thursday. The S&P 500 lost 2.02% to 7,175.8, its sixth straight fall, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% to 23,879.2 and the Dow shed 1,101 points (2.19%) to finish below 50,000. Anthropic's listing, priced at US$83 a share and the largest IPO on record, opened at US$111.50 and closed well above its offer price, but it failed to lift the wider AI trade. Chip makers fell broadly, with Nvidia down for a sixth session, and Walmart slipped after its annual sales forecast disappointed. The VIX volatility index rose about 15% to 28.4.

commentary.heading: Jobs shock extends the ASX losing streak
commentary.body: The ASX 200 fell 1.04% to 8,730.4 on Thursday, a sixth straight loss. Unemployment jumped to 4.9% in October, the highest since 2021, as employment fell by 43,500 when a gain had been expected. Materials led the declines, down 3.7%, as overnight falls in copper and gold hit miners: South32 lost 5.9%, Rio Tinto 4.1%, BHP 3.7% and Northern Star 5.7%. Energy fell 2.1%. Technology, health care and communication services rose, helped by Telstra, NextDC and Sonic Healthcare, while a2 Milk dropped 11.7%.

commentary.heading: Asia and London lower
commentary.body: Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.95% to 22,841.6. Mainland shares also eased, with the Shanghai Composite down 0.28% to 3,577.6 and the Shenzhen Component down 0.71% to 10,583.2, as trading volumes thinned. In London the FTSE 100 lost 0.93% to 10,452.7 as selling picked up late in the session; Babcock rose after strong half-year results, while JD Sports fell after trimming its profit guidance.

commentary.heading: Central banks and inflation
commentary.body: The weak jobs figures shifted expectations for the RBA: markets moved from pricing possible further hikes to pricing a cut in 2027, although the cash rate of 4.85% is still expected to be held in December. In the US, futures pricing points to a high chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December after hawkish meeting minutes. The federal funds range remains 3.75–4.00% and the Bank of England rate 4.00%.

commentary.heading: Bonds, oil and the Australian dollar
commentary.body: Australia's 10-year yield fell 11 basis points to 4.98%, its lowest in about three months, after the jobs data. The US 10-year eased to 5.05%, while the UK 10-year edged up to 5.32%. US crude rose 1% to US$83.13 a barrel and gold fell about 2%. The Australian dollar dropped to around 66.6 US cents, its lowest level this year.

commentary.heading: What to watch
commentary.body: China sets its loan prime rates today, after 17 months without change. Next week brings Australia's October monthly CPI and the US PCE inflation measure, and US markets close on Thursday for Thanksgiving. The RBA meets on 8 December and the Fed on 9 December.
